prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.62
  gal: 0.38
</profile>

TEXT_C:
Summary of key proposals (2017 manifesto), stripped of ideological framing:

Brexit and sovereignty
- Six tests for exit: regain full lawmaking supremacy outside the ECJ/ECHR; full control of immigration and borders; restore a 200‑mile Exclusive Economic Zone and national fisheries control; exit the single market and customs union and regain independent WTO seat; no “divorce” payment and recover UK assets held in EU bodies; complete by end‑2019.
- Preferred method: repeal the European Communities Act 1972; maintain EU-derived laws temporarily, then amend/repeal.
- Fisheries: leave the Common Fisheries Policy; revoke the 1964 London Convention; land all fish caught in UK waters in the UK; create a Fisheries Protection Force.

Public finances and tax
- Reallocate c. £35bn by reducing foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, cancelling HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula with needs-based funding, and ending EU payments.
- Tax changes: raise personal allowance to £13,500 and 40% threshold to £55,000; increase inheritance tax threshold to £500,000 per person; abolish TV licence; remove VAT from domestic energy, hot takeaway food, and sanitary products; freeze Insurance Premium Tax.
- Crack down on multinational profit-shifting.

Business, jobs, and coastal revival
- Cut business rates 20% for premises with RV <£50k; penalise serial late payers; open public procurement to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns for the self‑employed.
- Require UK-first job advertising; tighten zero-hours use; enforce minimum/living wage.
- Create coastal enterprise zones with 50% rates cuts and housing/enforcement measures.

Housing
- Establish a Housing Development Corporation to build up to 100,000 factory‑built modular homes annually on brownfield sites for first‑time buyers under 40; resale back to HDC at cost+inflation; expand council housebuilding; review housing associations.

Health and social care
- By 2021/22: +£9bn/year for NHS England and +£2bn/year for social care.
- Lift medical school cap to 10,000; fund tuition for doctors/nurses with service commitments; expand GP and support roles; end 1% pay cap below Band 6.
- Integrate NHS and social care in a single department; restrict non‑urgent NHS access to citizens or those contributing taxes for five years; strengthen cost recovery; license NHS managers; limit consultancy spend; end PFI; scrap hospital parking charges.

Mental health
- +£500m/year; 28‑day maximum wait; school-based counselling nationwide; integrated support for forces personnel and veterans.

Education and skills
- Expand selective and technical schools; abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; primary languages; restore maintenance grants.
- Abolish tuition fees for STEM and medical students with UK service commitments; embed employability and entrepreneurship; protect special educational needs provision.

Welfare, elderly, disability
- Maintain pensioner benefits and triple lock; up to £2bn/year extra for social care; fair contracts and travel-time pay for care workers.
- Dementia plan with £400m/year; reform PIP and Work Capability Assessments; increase Carer’s Allowance; optional direct rent payment to landlords.

Immigration and integration
- Target balanced net migration (near zero) over five years via points-based and work‑permit system; 5‑year moratorium on low‑skilled visas; seasonal schemes; 4,000 extra border staff.
- Visa holders to carry private medical insurance; five years’ contributions before most benefits/non‑urgent NHS; faster removal of foreign offenders; no amnesty.
- Pre‑Article 50 EU residents may remain; post‑date entrants lose automatic rights at exit.
- One law for all; disband parallel legal councils; measures against FGM, forced marriage, and “honour” crimes; face coverings banned in public places; stronger school oversight against extremism.

Policing, justice, defence, foreign policy
- +20,000 police; restore stop-and-search; +7,000 prison officers; reduce overcrowding; tougher prison drug and violence controls; segregate/prioritise deradicalisation where needed.
- Opt out of the European Arrest Warrant; UK Bill of Rights; tighter alcohol licensing; FOBT £2 stake cap.
- Defence: spend a genuine 2% of GDP plus +£1bn/year; +20,000 personnel; procurement reform; independent nuclear deterrent; veterans’ administration, housing, jobs guarantees; limit retrospective prosecutions.

Trade, aid, and global role
- Reduce aid to 0.2% of GNI; close standalone aid department; focus on disaster relief, health, water; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship.
- Pursue global FTAs; accept WTO terms if needed; support value‑adding exports from developing nations.

Transport, environment, farming, energy, democracy, localism
- Scrap HS2; improve existing rail (esp. east‑west in the North); remove road tolls; expand EV charging; protect diesel owners from new penalties; support regional airports; freeze then cut Air Passenger Duty.
- New Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodlands; brownfield first; plastic bottle deposit scheme.
- Replace CAP with UK farm payments capped at £120k, paid to active farmers; boost organic/hill farms; support antibiotic‑free livestock; ban live exports for slaughter; CCTV in abattoirs; clear slaughter labelling; tougher animal cruelty penalties.
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; leave Paris Agreement and EU ETS; diversify energy mix including shale (not in protected areas); cut domestic and industrial energy costs.
- Abolish the upper chamber; create an English Parliament; halve Commons to 325 elected by proportional representation; restrict postal voting to need; binding citizen‑initiated referenda; local binding referenda; strengthen committee governance in councils; cut local waste and costs.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals (ideology removed)

Economy, tax, trade, regulation
- Balance the budget by the mid-2020s; keep taxes low; raise personal allowance to £12,500 and higher-rate threshold to £50,000 by 2020; no VAT rise; cut corporation tax to 17%; simplify taxes and reform business rates with more frequent revaluations.
- Replicate existing EU trade agreements; lodge UK WTO schedules; create nine regional Trade Commissioners and reconvene the Board of Trade; introduce a Trade Bill.
- Cut unnecessary regulation; review utility and transport regulation to improve value.
- Raise the National Living Wage to 60% of median earnings by 2020 and thereafter with median pay; strengthen protections for gig-economy workers (post‑Taylor Review).
- Toughen action on tax evasion/avoidance; empower HMRC on smuggling and online VAT fraud.

Corporate governance, pensions, takeovers
- Annual binding shareholder votes on executive pay; publish pay ratios; examine share buybacks.
- Require employee voice in listed company boards (options-based).
- Strengthen Pensions Regulator: block risky deals, levy punitive fines, consider a new criminal offence.

Industrial strategy, R&D, skills, SMEs
- National Productivity Investment Fund (£23bn); R&D to 2.4% of GDP in 10 years (goal 3%); expand university investment funds; create “Future Britain” sovereign-style funds.
- Align visas to strategic skills needs; double Immigration Skills Charge to £2,000; keep net migration to the tens of thousands.
- 33% of central procurement from SMEs; enforce Prompt Payment; consider energy tariff cap for micro‑businesses.

Energy and environment
- Independent review to cut energy costs; industrial energy efficiency scheme; safeguard tariff cap for households; universal smart meter offer by 2020.
- Support offshore wind and Scottish island projects; limit large onshore wind in England.
- Develop UK shale with a new regulator, planning changes, and community payments.
- 25‑year environment plan; tree planting; anti‑litter and air quality measures; Blue Belt marine protections.

Transport and infrastructure
- Proceed with HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow; major roads upgrades; EV strategy (aim near‑zero-emission cars/vans by 2050); more low‑emission buses; cycling expansion; increase rail capacity and introduce passenger ombudsman.

Union, devolution, communities
- Reject a new Scottish independence referendum “at this time”; expand city and growth deals (e.g., Borderlands, North Wales); relocate civil service and Channel 4 outside London; United Kingdom Shared Prosperity Fund to replace EU structural funds.
- Extend Coastal Communities Fund; new post‑CFP fisheries regime; withdraw from London Fisheries Convention.
- Rural: maintain farm support cash totals to 2022 and design new agri‑environment schemes; mandatory CCTV in slaughterhouses; enhance post office banking access; free vote on the Hunting Act.

Brexit and law
- Leave the single market and customs union; seek a comprehensive free trade and customs agreement; Great Repeal Bill to convert EU law; maintain Common Travel Area; protect Gibraltar; final deal vote in both Houses.
- No EU Charter of Fundamental Rights in UK law; remain ECHR signatory this parliament.

Security, defence, justice, immigration
- Maintain defence at ≥2% of GDP and rise 0.5% above inflation annually; retain nuclear deterrent; major equipment investments; veterans’ Board and NI holiday for hires.
- Merge SFO into NCA; create a national infrastructure police force; expand cyber security; victims’ law; prison reform with 10,000 places; tougher community sentences; provision for women offenders.
- Reduce net migration; raise family visa income thresholds; tighten student visa rules; expect students to leave unless meeting higher requirements; keep students in migration stats.
- Asylum focus on resettlement from regions in need; review international definitions.

Education and skills
- 100+ new free schools/year; university and independent school sponsorship; lift ban on new selective schools (with conditions); ease rules for new Catholic schools; specialist maths schools; admissions review (no lottery); EBacc expansion; curriculum/teacher support; national jobs portal.
- School funding reform with no school losing cash; increase budget by £4bn by 2022; replace universal infant lunches with universal primary breakfasts; protect Pupil Premium.
- Technical education: new T‑levels, 900 hours/year, 3‑month placements; institutes of technology; FE investment; 3m apprenticeships; levy flexibility; UCAS‑style portal; discounted travel for apprentices; national retraining scheme; right to request training leave.

NHS, social care, pensions, cost of living, housing
- NHS: minimum £8bn real-terms increase over five years; more staff training; invest in buildings/IT; verify eligibility and raise Immigration Health Surcharge; faster access to innovations; 7‑day services; retain A&E 95% and 18‑week standards; expand mental health workforce by up to 10,000; faster cancer diagnosis (28 days); improve learning disability/autism and end‑of‑life care.
- Social care: include home value in means test for home care; £100,000 asset floor; extend deferred payments to home care; means‑test Winter Fuel Payments; statutory carer’s leave; green paper on system reform.
- State pension: keep triple lock to 2020; then “double lock” (earnings or inflation); align pension age with life expectancy; expand auto‑enrolment (incl. self‑employed).
- Consumers: stronger regulators; fairer telecoms billing; tackle leasehold abuses; modernise homebuying; longer tenancies; rail ticketing simplification; minimum rail service levels during strikes; “Breathing Space” for problem debt.
- Housing: 1.5m homes by 2022; protect Green Belt/valued landscapes; government to build 160,000 homes; modern construction; capture land value; council housing deals to build fixed‑term social homes with Right to Buy after 10–15 years; CPO reform; specialist and flood‑resilient housing.

Digital
- Digital Charter; new data protection law; Data Use and Ethics Commission; right for young adults to delete social media data; £1.9bn cyber programme; Verify digital ID rollout; open data expansion; broadband USO by 2020; full‑fibre spines in 100+ towns by 2022; majority 5G coverage by 2027; 95% geographic mobile coverage by 2022; Wi‑Fi on mainline trains; geospatial data body.
- Stronger online safety rules (minors’ protections, counter‑terror content); international cooperation and potential industry levy to address internet harms.
- End Leveson 2; repeal Section 40; ensure sustainable online media business models.
